The suturing of the nasal septum after septoplasty can be considered as an alternative to nasal packing. While both methods aim to manage symptoms and reduce congestion, there are distinct advantages and disadvantages associated with each approach.

Septal suturing offers several benefits, including elimination of discomfort for patients, minimal complications, a similar outcome in terms of symptom resolution, and a reduced hospital stay compared to nasal packing. This procedure allows for direct application of the suture material under magnification, which can lead to more precise placement and better healing outcomes.

On the other hand, nasal packing provides an immediate release of pressure from the nasal cavity and has been shown to be effective in reducing symptoms in some cases. However, it may not eliminate discomfort for patients, has a slightly higher risk of complications, and requires a longer hospital stay compared to suturing.

In summary, while both methods have their own merits, septal suturing after septoplasty can be considered an effective alternative to nasal packing due to its advantages in terms of symptom management, complication reduction, and shorter hospital stay. However, it's essential to consider individual patient needs and circumstances when deciding between these two approaches.
